proposal.description_long: President Donald Trump removed State Department Inspector General Steve Linick in May 2020. The congressional record and the congressional inquiry into the removal document that Linick’s office had several open matters involving Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, including review of the emergency arms-sale process and a separate inquiry concerning use of department staff for personal tasks. Lawmakers said they were investigating whether the dismissal was retaliatory. That allegation must remain attributed: the existence of pending inquiries and the timing of the removal do not by themselves prove motive. Pompeo said he recommended Linick’s removal and denied knowing about one investigation; the White House’s notification cited the president’s lack of confidence. The source URL attached to this row is an unrelated 2026 Oklahoma wildfire forecast and supplies no evidence for the personnel action. Replace it with the congressional records or contemporaneous reporting before publication. A defensible description can state the removal and the documented oversight context while distinguishing the competing accounts of the reason.
